title: Steve Jobs
author: Walter Isaacson
review: Klassiker. Steve Jobs inspired me in many ways: in life choices, in art and design, in how people perceive things, and in his way of telling stories. What I liked most is how human the book makes him. Someone I could relate to, and someone whose flaws I could see.

title: The Hard Thing About Hard Things
author: Ben Horowitz
review: Ben Horowitz took an angle on explaining the difficulties of leading people that I hadn't read before. He answered many questions that seem too difficult to answer, and introduced many ideas I didn't have before (e.g. the wartime vs. peacetime CEO). Also, his connection to rap is goated.

title: Made to Stick
author: Chip Heath & Dan Heath
review: Great book. For many people these techniques are obvious, but when I read this book at 18, it helped me understand what makes good presentations good. Since then I always try to evoke some kind of emotion in my speeches, and there always is one, even if you are talking about calculus.

title: Talk Like TED
author: Carmine Gallo
review: My main takeaway (and this is so true for me): practice presenting every chance you get. Everybody has a great presentation in theory, but only in theory. When it is actually time to present, people mess up. There are many things you can do to get better, but by far the best one is to just present every chance you get.

title: Notes on Being a Man
author: Scott Galloway
review: Scott Galloway is a mentor of mine. This book shaped a lot of what I'm doing, and with this book and his podcast he gave and still gives me direction on who I want to be. Thanks to my friend Niklas for telling me about Scott when I was 18. 10/10, would read again.

title: The Great Work of Your Life
author: Stephen Cope
review: I often tell friends: I'm happy if a book gives me one message that lasts, even if I forget 99% of what's in it. That describes this book very well. The one message for me: there are times in your life when you live for one purpose, and only one. You know it while you're in it. And those months or years build who you are more than anything else.
